paper.central_claim: Training-Free GRPO shifts policy optimization from parameter space to context space: a frozen LLM's group-relative semantic advantage over rollouts is distilled into an evolving experience library (token prior) with add/delete/modify/keep operations, improving out-of-domain AIME and WebWalkerQA performance with ~100 training samples at tens of dollars and outperforming fine-tuned small LLMs.
paper.title: Training-Free Group Relative Policy Optimization

signatures.object: Experience library E (<=32-word natural-language experiences) injected into the prompt of a frozen policy LLM
signatures.information: G rollouts per query under E, rewards from ground-truth answers (or none in the no-GT variant), per-rollout LLM summaries
signatures.operation: Skip uniform-reward groups; LLM extracts group-relative semantic advantage; batch-level LLM proposes add/delete/modify/keep (and merge) edits to E; repeat for 3 epochs
signatures.output: Updated library E that conditions subsequent rollouts and the final deployment prompt
signatures.conditions: 100 training queries (DAPO-100 or AFM-100), group size 5 (math) / 3 (web), temperature 0.7
signatures.feedback: Ground-truth reward (math, web) or implicit majority-vote/self-discrimination (no-GT ablation)
signatures.selection_rule: LLM-judged edits; no held-out acceptance test; train-set Mean@5 tracked (Fig 4)
signatures.persistence: Library text (48 experiences in the math run) reused at inference
signatures.claimed_effect: ReAct+CI AIME24/25 +2.7/+5.4; WebWalkerQA +4.6; beats count-matched generated experiences
signatures.failure_boundary: Weak models (QwQ-32B) degrade; no-GT variant gains only ~+1; relies on base-model tool use

gap.author_gap: Parameter-space agentic RL is costly, data-hungry, poorly generalizing and limited to small models; can agent performance improve non-parametrically?
gap.checked_gap: Real for deployments on API models; however, cross-sample experience libraries (Agent KB, Dynamic Cheatsheet, ExpeL-type stores) already learn non-parametrically, so the open delta is group-relative multi-epoch library optimisation.
gap.lineage: In-context learning / Reflexion / Self-Refine / TextGrad (within-sample) -> Agent KB (cross-task library) -> Training-Free GRPO (GRPO-shaped multi-epoch library optimization).
closest_adjacent: Dynamic Cheatsheet/ACE-type playbooks (not discussed in material)
gap.residue: Direct comparison with other training-free memories at equal budget and with GRPO on the same base is absent.
gap.stakes: $18 and 100 samples vs about $10,000 RL replication.
gap.method_response: Group-relative semantic advantage and add/delete/modify edit operations on a frozen model.
gap.remaining_gap: Same-base RL comparison, other training-free baselines, library maintenance/gating.
unresolved: Nearest-neighbor playbook/memory papers not pinned locally

claims.text: Training-Free GRPO significantly improves a frozen DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus on out-of-domain AIME and WebWalkerQA with ~100 samples.
claims.setting: AIME24/25 Mean@32 (direct and ReAct+CI), WebWalkerQA pass@1; learning on DAPO-100/AFM-100
claims.baseline_control: ReAct baseline; count-matched generated experiences; w/o GT; w/o group
claims.selection_vs_test: Separate training sets from the evaluation benchmarks; AIME monitored per step
claims.result_denominator: ReAct +2.7/+5.4; direct +4.0/+1.1; web +4.6 (63.2->67.8); no intervals; AIME 30 problems each
claims.allowed_conclusion: A short learned experience library lifts a strong frozen model by a few points on held-out benchmarks in single runs; the no-GT variant gains about 1 point.

claims.text: Training-Free GRPO outperforms RL-fine-tuned 32B models at a fraction of the cost.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A frozen 671B model with a short experience library beats RL-trained 32B models cheaply to train; this reflects the larger base more than the method and is not a same-base comparison.

claims.text: Group-relative computation and ground-truth guidance are necessary.
claims.setting: Table 2 (AIME) and Table 5 (WebWalkerQA subset n=51, 2 epochs)
claims.baseline_control: group size 1; no GT; directly generated experiences
claims.allowed_conclusion: Directionally supported on AIME; web ablation differences are one or two problems.

claims.text: Superior generalization: plugging in domain experiences avoids the domain-specialization trade-off.
claims.result_denominator: ReTool web 18.3; TF-GRPO 67.8 on a 671B base
claims.allowed_conclusion: Not tested for the method: no cross-domain library transfer and no same-base comparison.

assessment.evidence_level_note: A library learned on 100 separate samples improves held-out benchmarks and beats a count-matched self-generated library; no improver-level evidence.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A 3-step, 100-sample, ~$18 group-relative LLM-reflection loop builds a 48-item experience library that raises frozen DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus by +2.7/+5.4 (AIME24/25, ReAct+CI) and +4.6 (WebWalkerQA), beating count-matched unoptimized experiences; comparisons with RL-trained 32B models and cross-domain superiority are confounded by base model and untested.

G.reason: Real practical gap (RL cost/data scarcity) but the 'frozen model improves from text' premise is the stated novelty; nearest cross-task experience libraries (Agent KB; DC/ExpeL-style, not named) are separated only verbally and not run.

M.reason: Semantic group advantage and library edit operations are well-specified and the group/GT ablations are directionally consistent, but the GRPO equivalence and KL-like stability are analogies, and generalization/overfitting advantages over parametric RL are asserted.

X.reason: Rollout, summary, extraction and add/delete/modify/keep+merge steps with full prompts are reproducible; no acceptance test of library updates on held-out data, no versioning/rollback, and the stopping point is unexplained.

E.measurement.reason: AIME answer-matching Mean@32 is a trustworthy metric; the reward/verifier for learning and the WebWalkerQA judge and test size are not specified, and web ablations use 51 items.

E.causality.reason: Count-matched self-generated experiences, w/o GT and w/o group computation controls on AIME; but the headline comparison to RL-trained 32B models confounds base model (80.0/67.9 untrained vs 67.0/49.3), no same-base GRPO, no other training-free memory baseline, web ablations at n=51.

E.holdout.reason: Learning on DAPO-100/AFM-100 and testing on AIME/WebWalkerQA is a clean source/target split, but AIME was monitored at each step, contamination of DAPO vs AIME is unexamined, and the cross-domain generalization claim is not tested on a same-base comparison.

E.statistics.reason: Mean@32 reduces decoding noise on small benchmarks, but each variant is one learned library from one 100-sample draw with no seeds or intervals; web ablation differences are one problem.

E.cost.reason: Learning tokens/hours/dollars and per-problem inference cost are stated and compared to an RL replication cost, with inference cost disclosed as higher than a dedicated 32B; excludes hyperparameter/failed trials.

evidence.quote: Is applying RL in parametric space the only viable approach? Can we enhance LLM agent performance in a non-parametric way with lower data and computational costs?
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap is the cost/data scarcity of parameter-space agentic RL; 'no weight update' is the premise.

evidence.quote: we argue that LLMs can achieve a similar effect on the output distribution by learning experiential knowledge as a token prior
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: experiential knowledge as a token prior replaces GRPO's output-distribution shift.

evidence.quote: we generate such semantic advantages only for groups with both clear winners and losers.
evidence.support_explanation: Groups with identical rewards are skipped, mirroring GRPO's zero advantage.

evidence.quote: produces a shifted output distribution in subsequent batches or epochs. This mirrors the effect of a GRPO policy update by steering the model towards higher-reward outputs, but achieves this by altering the context rather than the model’s fundamental parameters.
evidence.support_explanation: Equivalence to GRPO is stated by analogy, not derived or measured on the same base model.

evidence.quote: remove a low-quality experience from the experience library
evidence.support_explanation: Library edit operations include Add, Delete, Modify, Keep (and Merge in the optimization prompt, App B).

evidence.support_explanation: Claimed stability analogue of the KL term; no test of drift or harmful-update rollback.
